procedure.description: intensity modulated radiation therapy planning, left breast after lumpectomy

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 77301 (intensity modulated radiation therapy planning, left breast after lumpectomy) with date of service 2026-09-02. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Intensity modulated radiation therapy is not medically necessary for breast cancer; three-dimensional conformal radiation therapy is the covered standard.

criteria.text: Adjuvant radiation to the intact breast or chest wall after surgery for invasive breast carcinoma.

A three-dimensional conformal plan was generated and documented to exceed normal-tissue dose constraints (mean heart dose above 4 Gy, or ipsilateral lung V20 above 20 percent), such that intensity modulated planning is required to meet them.
Target volume, dose, and fractionation documented by the treating radiation oncologist.

chart.text: Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Blood pressure check. 135 over 84 today, 123 over 76 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Vitamin D came back 24. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
A1c came back 5.9. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.

Left breast lumpectomy and sentinel node biopsy: 1.7 centimeter grade 2 invasive ductal carcinoma, margins negative, closest 3 millimeters, 0 of 2 sentinel nodes, estrogen receptor positive, HER2 negative.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 220, LDL 127, HDL 38, triglycerides 133. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 19 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

47 year old woman in radiation oncology consultation. Reviewed the role of whole-breast radiation after lumpectomy, hypofractionation, and the left-sided heart question. She is anxious about the heart and asked good questions. Her history otherwise: hypertension on lisinopril. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Quit smoking 12 years ago, no alcohol, stays home with the kids. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Status post left lumpectomy for a 1.7 centimeter invasive ductal carcinoma, node negative. Adjuvant whole-breast radiation recommended, then endocrine therapy.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Follow-up to answer questions with her husband. Reviewed the breath-hold technique we will try at simulation. Consent signed. Vitals today 135 over 89, pulse 80.

Simulation. Supine on the breast board, left arm up, deep inspiration breath hold attempted and reproducible to 3 millimeters. CT acquired, isocenter set, skin marks placed. Heart sits close to the chest wall even in breath hold.

Comparative plans, left breast, 42.56 Gy in 16 fractions. Three-dimensional conformal tangents with a heart block: mean heart dose 6.1 Gy, left anterior descending maximum 41 Gy, ipsilateral lung V20 22 percent. The 3D plan fails the heart constraint. Intensity modulated plan: mean heart dose 2.4 Gy, lung V20 13 percent, target coverage 95 percent of the volume at 95 percent of the dose. IMRT required to meet constraints.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Treatment planning note. Prescription: whole left breast 42.56 Gy in 16 fractions of 2.66 Gy, lumpectomy cavity boost 10 Gy in 4 fractions. Target volumes contoured on the simulation scan, plan reviewed and approved today.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
